short: Parliament's radical, professionally organized military force that won the civil wars and executed sweeping political changes.
full:
Formed in February 1645 by the English Parliament, the New Model Army replaced localized, often reluctant militias with a unified, professional standing army. Sir Thomas Fairfax was appointed its commander-in-chief, with officers promoted based on military competence and puritan zeal rather than aristocratic birth. Backed by guaranteed central funding and equipped with standardized red uniforms, the army rapidly became a highly disciplined and formidable fighting force.

The New Model Army decisively crushed Royalist forces at Naseby only months after its creation. Following the defeat of the king, the army became a powerful political entity in its own right, highly politicized by radical ideas and religious fervor. It subsequently purged Parliament, facilitated the execution of Charles I, and served as the fundamental instrument of power throughout the Protectorate until its disbandment after the 1660 Restoration.
